rv.q: O’Hara is superb: she brings warmth, mischief and vibrant intelligence to the part.
Sher’s production gives deep pleasure and will make you think twice about patronising this show in future.
Kelli O’Hara’s performance as this widowed teacher has a radiant charm and intelligence.
Having stood to join the inevitable ovation, you’ll head out into the night whistling a very happy tune.
In old-fashioned Broadway terms, the production looks and sounds ravishing – it has a splendour that lets punters see where their money (top ticket prices are steep) has been spent.
Thanks to Miss O'Hara, this is a night of old-fashioned glamour.
Anyhoo, the pedigree of Bartlett Sher's production is pretty immaculate.
The musical itself, however, remains, a problem to be solved as much as a show to be enjoyed.
The lavish design looks as opulent as an oriental palace in the mid nineteenth century should.
It is a great addition to the summer theatrical roster for the West End.
This is also a golden production that revels in spectacle, supported by a full-blooded orchestra making a beguiling case for this classic score.
This is undeniably a beautiful revival, created with care, respect and skill and as a result, it is mostly simply a joy to watch.

Though there are times where it's quite difficult to understand Watanabe's words - unfortunately, including a potentially entertaining number ('A Puzzlement') - he more than makes up for it in charisma, humour and a magnetic stage presence.
Both Watanabe and O’Hara succeed in making two very famous characters multi-faceted.

cn.t: Bartlett Sher's Tony-winning revival dazzles with blazing beauty and lush spectacle. Kelli O'Hara delivers a radiant, Tony-winning performance, while Ken Watanabe brings magnetic charisma to the King in this glorious, visually stunning production.
